subject.title: Add multi-gateway cron job coordination for HA deployments

question: Should distributed cron ownership be a core feature, a plugin-provided coordination API, or deferred to the broader horizontal-scaling/runtime work?
rationale: The code gap is clear, but choosing the backend boundary, config shape, failure semantics, and relationship to broader HA architecture is a maintainer product decision.

options.title: Design backend-neutral ownership
options.body: Define a generic cron lease/leader contract before implementation so Redis, etcd, DynamoDB, or SQLite-backed deployments do not become competing one-off paths.

options.title: Fold into broader HA RFC
options.body: Treat this as a cron-specific requirement under the open horizontal-scaling or distributed-runtime issues and close only after that canonical design explicitly owns cron scheduling.

options.title: Document external-only pattern
options.body: If core should stay single-Gateway for cron, document external scheduler/lock patterns and explicitly mark HA cron coordination out of scope.

recommendation.title: Design backend-neutral ownership
recommendation.body: Define a generic cron lease/leader contract before implementation so Redis, etcd, DynamoDB, or SQLite-backed deployments do not become competing one-off paths.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest recent cron scheduler history and already supplied the prior architecture-review routing for this issue.
